items.title: Four questions to help you stop overthinking
items.content_snippet: Overthinking feels productive, and that is exactly the trap the research pins down. items.title: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol now supports Ultrafast mode on Amazon Bedrock
items.content_snippet: Today, AWS announces the availability of Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol from OpenAI on Amazon Bedrock. Ultrafast mode provides faster inference for workloads where speed matters most. The Amazon Bedrock inference engine delivers the performance, security, and reliability required for production workloads. Use GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast for latency-sensitive applications such as real-time coding assistants, interactive agents, and customer-facing experiences that require fast, high-quality responses.

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports minor version upgrade prechecks and a new RDS event to help reduce patching downtime
items.content_snippet: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now lets you run a minor version upgrade precheck yourself, before you start an upgrade or before your scheduled maintenance window. RDS for Oracle now also emits a new event during patching that tells you when your DB instance is accepting connections again. items.title: Stop Prompting — Greg Pstrucha, Sentry
items.content_snippet: You correct your agent. It says "You're absolutely right." Five minutes later, after compaction, it makes the same mistake again. items.title: How a Remote Company Builds AI Fluency — Em Shreve, Automattic
items.content_snippet: Handing people AI tools doesn't change how they work. Giving them real time to learn does. Em Shreve, head of AI enablement at Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com and Tumblr with over 1,400 people in 82 countries, explains how a fully remote company builds AI fluency. items.content_snippet: Coding agents are great inside one repo. Postman has 115 microservices and thousands of endpoints. Kamalakannan Nandagopal, staff engineer at Postman, shares how Postman made coding agents work across a real distributed system. Docs go stale, skills and MCPs are only as good as their context, and agent memory stays stuck with one person. items.title: Turning Agent Memory Into Skills That Work — Will Lyon, Neo4j
items.content_snippet: Agents finish a task, then forget what they learned. Retrieval alone won't fix that. Will Lyon, senior product manager at Neo4j, explains why agent memory built on embeddings and retrieval isn't enough: recall isn't actionable knowledge. Agents need knowledge that is connected, typed and traceable. items.title: Your AI Agent Has No Nervous System — Matt Gibiec, Dynatrace
items.content_snippet: Your coding agent is fast. But it can't see how your services actually run, so it guesses. Matt Gibiec, who leads AI-native solutions engineering at Dynatrace, explains why AI agents need something like a nervous system: real context from the environment they're changing. Agents get stuck in loops, cause operational and security issues, and are hard to measure, because they work fast but blind, only as good as the data they can see.
